answer: Registration locks a locked liquidity-pool share as a slashable bond: an identity costs real money. The network catches selling an identity to a new operator through key-rotation monitors. Once the fault is proven, half the bond is slashed and the rest frozen for ten epochs. No identity exists without its own velvet of locked funds. A farm needs a fresh meadow per fake, each costing a full bond. Without a falcon of fresh stake, a new identity cannot register.
